# Gamehaus’s Anamana agreement separates seller payments from business funding


By OpenTools Team


Shares for existing owners and new company cash serve different purposes.


##


Two recipients, two payment forms


[Gamehaus’s November 2 agreement](https://ir.gamehaus.com/2026-11-02-Gamehaus-Signs-Definitive-Agreement-to-Acquire-Majority-Stake-in-Anamana) would pay existing Techforge shareholders US$19.6 million in Gamehaus shares, with no cash to sellers. They include an entity controlled by Gamehaus founder and chairman Feng Xie—a related‑party seller relationship.


Separately, US$7 million in new cash would enter Techforge, Anamana’s holding company. Buying existing ownership and funding the business are different capital flows.


##


Control remains conditional


[Together, the steps](https://ir.gamehaus.com/2026-11-02-Gamehaus-Signs-Definitive-Agreement-to-Acquire-Majority-Stake-in-Anamana) would give Gamehaus approximately 56% of Techforge. Gamehaus plans to add Anamana’s AI‑assisted serialized‑video production and distribution to its gaming portfolio.


Closing is expected in November 2026, subject to customary conditions; the signed agreement does not establish completed ownership.
